details.description: Command (Amazon Bedrock model ID cohere.command-text-v14) is Cohere's original instruction-following conversational model. Cohere deprecated and shut down this legacy 'command' model on September 15, 2025, directing users to command-r-08-2024, command-r-plus-08-2024, or command-a-03-2025 instead, and it no longer appears among the Cohere models Amazon Bedrock's current model catalog lists (Command R, Command R+, Embed, and Rerank models only). It supports a 4,096-token context window with up to 4,096 output tokens over a text-only chat endpoint.
advantages: Cohere describes it as an instruction-following conversational model that performs language tasks with higher quality, more reliably, and with longer context than Cohere's base generative models.
disadvantages: Deprecated and shut down by Cohere on September 15, 2025; Cohere directs users to command-r-08-2024, command-r-plus-08-2024, or command-a-03-2025 instead.
No longer offered as a current model in Cohere's own model list or in Amazon Bedrock's current Cohere model catalog.
4,096-token context window and 4,096-token output limit, far smaller than Cohere's current Command models (128K-256K context).
No function/tool-calling support noted for this model.
use_cases: General-purpose instruction-following chat and text generation, per Cohere's description of the model.

notes: Catalog's facts (4,096 max input and max output tokens) match Cohere's documented context/output limits for the legacy 'command' model. Catalog's deprecation_date fact is empty, but Cohere's own deprecations page and its Sept 15 2025 changelog state this model (API name 'command', Bedrock ID cohere.command-text-v14, per Cohere's own docs/models page) was deprecated and shut down 2025-09-15; it is also absent from AWS Bedrock's current Cohere model-cards listing (fetched twice, consistently). The two URIs in this group (1-month-commitment and 6-month-commitment) are the same underlying model under different Bedrock Provisioned Throughput commitment terms, not different models, so they were described together.
